post.description: User login (returns JWT token and sets refresh cookie).

User logout.

- Clears the ``refresh_token`` HttpOnly cookie.
- If a Bearer access token is present in the Authorization header, adds it
  to the Redis blacklist so ``get_current_user`` rejects it immediately
  (before JWT expiry).
- Revokes the whole session family, so everything else minted under the
  same ``sid`` dies with it.

That last one is what makes the button mean what it says. Blacklisting the
two tokens in the request left every sibling of the session answering: the
access token an earlier rotation handed out is still inside its half-hour,
and the revoked refresh cookie was even forgiven by the rotation grace
window, which cannot tell a deliberate logout from a double-mount race.
The family marker can, and every path now reads it.

Admins are sent the full catalog rather than their (usually empty) grants,

that hid actions the API would happily perform would be lying.

Refresh JWT token using HttpOnly cookie.

Implements refresh token rotation: the old refresh token is blacklisted
and a new one is issued. Reuse of a blacklisted refresh token triggers
revocation of the entire token family for that user, unless the reuse
occurs within a short grace window (concurrent requests from React
StrictMode double-mount, mobile reloads, or multi-tab scenarios).

A caller with no cookie at all is not refused: the boot probe asks this
on every load before a session exists and "no session" is its ordinary
answer, not an error. The refusal cases (unreadable, revoked, expired)
stay 401 — those are answers about a session that existed.

are not rejected at response-serialization time.

must have a non-empty options list" because legacy data in
``categories.field_definitions`` JSONB was written before the rule existed
(e.g. system categories with ``equipment_status`` and ``options=[]``).

API write boundaries; the read model here accepts whatever the DB stored
so /items and /categories endpoints keep serializing legacy rows.

``preferred_language`` is the language the visitor was reading in; a new
sandbox's account takes it, so signing in does not switch the interface.

DocumentApprovalRequirement.title: DocumentApprovalRequirement
DocumentApprovalRequirement.description:
Whether confirming this document would send it to the approval queue.

The answer to the one rule (``document_gate.document_needs_approval_async``),
published so a screen about to confirm the document can name the
consequence instead of recomputing the rule from a workflow list and a
profile.

complete_as_planned.title: Complete As Planned
complete_as_planned.description: Complete without per-line answers: every line the body leaves unanswered is booked as delivered in full. Without this flag, a completion that leaves any line of a document other than a correction with no quantity and no discrepancy reason is refused, and the answer names those lines. A correction never needs it.

DocumentImportNoStockRow.title: DocumentImportNoStockRow
DocumentImportNoStockRow.description: A row whose line takes goods off a shelf that has none of it free.

DocumentLineTargetUpdate.title: DocumentLineTargetUpdate
DocumentLineTargetUpdate.description:
One receipt line's own destination. ``None`` clears the line's say —
the line goes back to following the rule and the document.

DocumentLineTracking.title: DocumentLineTracking
DocumentLineTracking.description:
The lot and expiry read off a pack for one receipt line.

A one-step posting books every line as planned, so it has no per-line
quantities to answer with — only the tracking the execution screen's
lot-and-expiry question collected. The values land on the line exactly
as a receiving scan's do.

DocumentListLineSchema.title: DocumentListLineSchema
DocumentListLineSchema.description: One of a list row's first lines: enough to say what moved.

DocumentListResponse.title: DocumentListResponse
DocumentListResponse.description:
Paginated document list — the canonical envelope.

Both endpoints already accepted ``limit``/``offset`` query params, so
``limit``, ``offset`` and ``has_more`` report real values rather than
invented ones.

DocumentListRowSchema.title: DocumentListRowSchema
DocumentListRowSchema.description:
A document as the documents list shows it, without its lines.

The list prints a sentence, a count and a progress bar per document; the
lines themselves are the document's own screen. Carried whole, they made
a page of fifty documents a megabyte. What the row needs from them is
summed here: ``line_count``, ``unit_progress`` and the first two lines
(``first_lines``), which name the product of a one-line document.
``module_lines`` are the lines a module's column can read — those that
carry fields of a module — and no others.

DocumentListUnitSchema.title: DocumentListUnitSchema
DocumentListUnitSchema.description: The unit a list line's quantity is printed in: its symbol and step.

DocumentModuleLineSchema.title: DocumentModuleLineSchema
DocumentModuleLineSchema.description: A line that carries a module's fields, as a module's list column reads it.

DocumentRowListResponse.title: DocumentRowListResponse
DocumentRowListResponse.description: A page of the documents list, one summed row per document.

DocumentStateDTO.title: DocumentStateDTO
DocumentStateDTO.description:
Where a document stands, for a module that may hold it.

``held_by`` names the module a document in ``PENDING_APPROVAL`` waits
for; empty on every document nothing holds. ``confirmed_by`` is who
submitted it, once it is confirmed.

DocumentSummary.title: DocumentSummary
DocumentSummary.description: Minimal document summary used in correction references.

DocumentType.title: DocumentType
DocumentType.description: Country-neutral by design — see ``document_types`` for the legacy map.

DocumentUnitProgressSchema.title: DocumentUnitProgressSchema
DocumentUnitProgressSchema.description:
What a document's lines in one unit planned and did, summed.

Kept per unit: 20 pcs and 12.5 kg are not 32.5 of anything.

DocumentsTodoDecisions.title: DocumentsTodoDecisions
DocumentsTodoDecisions.description:
What waits on a person's answer rather than on the floor's work.

Three kinds, each opening the screen where its decision is taken: a
backorder draft is confirmed or cancelled on its document, a document
waiting for approval is approved or rejected there, and goods in
quarantine are released or written off — a batch on its own screen, a
receipt's held quantity with the transfer or scrap off the quarantine
shelf. Reading this block decides nothing.

DocumentsTodoResponse.title: DocumentsTodoResponse
DocumentsTodoResponse.description:
To do's tasks, the two document lists they are partly built from, and
the decisions waiting on a person.

DocumentsTodoSection.title: DocumentsTodoSection
DocumentsTodoSection.description:
One side of the floor's queue: its rows and the server's own count.

The count describes every matching document, not the rows that fit in the
page — the two must agree when the queue is longer than one screen.

Not a pagination envelope on purpose (``docs/subsystems/PAGINATION.md``,
*Sections of a dashboard*): a section is one capped slice of a screen
that holds several of them, answered by one request. It has no page to
ask for, so ``limit``/``offset``/``has_more`` would promise a walk that
does not exist; the screen reads more than the cap from the document list.

EquipmentAssetItem.title: EquipmentAssetItem
EquipmentAssetItem.description:
Core Item payload extended with the equipment list columns.

``location_name`` and the open assignment's holder are filled by
the module list endpoint — they stay out of the core Item schema, which
must remain vertical-agnostic. The holder travels as a name plus its
kind (``person`` / ``location``): a deployment names the place, and the
reader words the two differently.

ExtraCostAllocation.title: ExtraCostAllocation
ExtraCostAllocation.description:
How one invoice is spread over the goods it arrived with.

``VALUE`` is the default because a shipment is usually charged in
proportion to what it is worth; ``WEIGHT`` is what a haulier actually
bills for; ``QUANTITY`` is the fallback that works when nobody typed a
price — such a line has an unknown cost basis, and a share of a total of
zero is a division by zero, not a cost.

ExtraCostKind.title: ExtraCostKind
ExtraCostKind.description:
What the extra invoice was for.

Countable, unlike a note. The four cover what a small importer actually
receives; anything else is OTHER with a note beside it.

ExtraCostLinePreview.title: ExtraCostLinePreview
ExtraCostLinePreview.description: What one line will cost once the delivery's own costs are on it.

FailedEmailSummary.title: FailedEmailSummary
FailedEmailSummary.description:
One message the queue gave up on, as the email screen lists them.

Deliberately not the body: an administrator answering for a message
that never arrived needs the address, the subject, when it was written
and what the relay said — not the rendered invitation itself, which on
this screen would only be a link anyone reading over their shoulder
could redeem.

FocusModeDiff.title: FocusModeDiff
FocusModeDiff.description:
The planned enabled-set delta for entering single-module focus mode.

Mirrors the profile-switch diff: ``disable``/``cascade_disable`` are what
switches off (with the cascade naming its reason in ``warnings``), and
``final_enabled_modules`` is the enabled set the mode settles on.

GeneratedProductCode.title: GeneratedProductCode
GeneratedProductCode.description: An internal EAN-13 for a product without a manufacturer's code.

HomeShelfOffer.title: HomeShelfOffer
HomeShelfOffer.description:
What a put-away says about the shelf the goods were put on.

``set``: the product has no home shelf and this one is offered. ``change``:
it has another and this one is offered in its place. ``refused``: this
shelf cannot be a home, and ``reason`` (``receiving``, ``quarantine`` or
``not_stock``) says why.

HomeShelfOut.title: HomeShelfOut
HomeShelfOut.description: The rule that now holds the product's home shelf, first on its list.

HomeShelfSet.title: HomeShelfSet
HomeShelfSet.description: The product and the shelf that becomes its home.

HomeShelfSilencedOut.title: HomeShelfSilencedOut
HomeShelfSilencedOut.description: A product whose put-away does not ask for a home shelf.

ImportDefaultsResult.title: ImportDefaultsResult
ImportDefaultsResult.description:
What an import did, row by row: a new ingredient, an override founded
over a system row, an existing override changed, or nothing.

mapping_json.title: Mapping Json
mapping_json.description: Column mapping (same shape as import-lines mapping_json).

create_stubs_for_unmatched.title: Create Stubs For Unmatched
create_stubs_for_unmatched.description: When True, unmatched barcodes auto-create a stub ProductTemplate so the line imports as matched.

ImportPreviewRow.title: ImportPreviewRow
ImportPreviewRow.description:
A single row from the import preview.

Columns are dynamic (driven by the source file's headers), so the row is
represented as a flat dict mapping column name → primitive value. The model
serialises back to the underlying dict, preserving the wire format the
frontend already expects.

IngredientAvailabilityItem.title: IngredientAvailabilityItem
IngredientAvailabilityItem.description: Per-ingredient availability in an availability check.

InheritedFieldDefinition.title: InheritedFieldDefinition
InheritedFieldDefinition.description: A custom field a location takes from a location above it.

InheritedTrackedField.title: InheritedTrackedField
InheritedTrackedField.description: A tracked field a location takes from a location above it.

InvitationCodeRequest.title: InvitationCodeRequest
InvitationCodeRequest.description:
Who the code is for, and what the account redeeming it becomes.

``role`` is the built-in base level; ``role_id`` optionally names an
org-scoped custom role the join assigns on top of it. ``email`` is the
address the code is bound to — only an account with that address can
redeem it.

InvitationSummary.title: InvitationSummary
InvitationSummary.description: One issued invitation, as the settings screen lists them.

ItemAggregates.title: ItemAggregates
ItemAggregates.description:
Totals over the whole filtered set, for the list footer.

The list paginates server-side, so its sums cannot come from the rows on
screen. ``weight`` is the ADR-015 derived line weight summed.
``total_volume`` is the same derivation's volume, in litres, summed
apart from the kilograms — a litre is not a kilogram, and one figure
labelled kilograms read 2 l of milk as 2 kg. A line counted in a volume
unit lands in ``total_volume``, by the rule ``Item.total_weight_unit``
applies per row. ``value`` is read where the statistics read it: from
the cost ledger, each record at its product's layer-average rate, where
the organization keeps one; from the price on each record where it does
not. ``value_source`` says which, and ``unpriced_count`` how many of
the counted rows the sum had nothing to price with. Rows without a
weight count toward ``count`` only.

The ledger answer exists only for the whole organization: its layers
know products, not shelves, so a filtered request gets ``total_value``
None and ``value_source`` ``not_available_under_filter`` — no figure,
rather than one priced at rates the other shelves earned. A filter on
a records-valued organization still gets its number, because there the
price sits on the very rows the filter keeps.

ItemImportJobResponse.title: ItemImportJobResponse
ItemImportJobResponse.description:
An import that runs on in the background, and how far it has got.

A sheet too long for one request is answered with this (HTTP 202) and
read again at ``GET /items/import/jobs/{id}`` until ``status`` is
``done`` — ``result`` then holds what the synchronous answer would have —
or ``failed``, with ``error`` saying why.

ItemImportResponse.title: ItemImportResponse
ItemImportResponse.description:
What one import did — including the org data it founded on the way.

A sheet may name locations and categories the organization does not
have yet; with auto-create on, the importer founds them. Their names
travel back so the reader learns what the file added beside the
products, instead of finding new tiles in the storage tree later.

``updated`` and ``skipped`` count the rows whose Label Code named a
product the organization already had, under the update mode the reader
chose; both stay zero when the import only adds.

``joined_existing`` counts the imported rows filed under a product that
already existed — by its barcode, or by its name and brand — and so added
stock to it rather than making a new product. A product two rows of one
sheet make together counts its second row here.

ItemListResponse.title: ItemListResponse
ItemListResponse.description:
Paginated response for the items list endpoint.

Concrete specialisation of PaginatedResponse[Item] — provides a stable
named type for OpenAPI schema generation and frontend TypeScript codegen.
Defaults maintained for backward compatibility.

ItemUseByRequest.title: ItemUseByRequest
ItemUseByRequest.description: The use-by of an opened package: a date, or ``null`` to clear it.

ItemUsePartiallyRequest.title: ItemUsePartiallyRequest
ItemUsePartiallyRequest.description:
What is left of a package, said in the unit the person sees on it.

``left`` absent only marks the package as opened. ``left_uom_id`` is the
unit ``left`` is in — the weight or volume on the bag; without it the
number is in the product's own unit (0.75 of a piece).

LabelAssignRequest.title: LabelAssignRequest
LabelAssignRequest.description: Data for quick product addition via scan

LabelCodeItem.title: LabelCodeItem
LabelCodeItem.description: A single explicit short_code to register in the LabelPool.

LabelFromCodesRequest.title: LabelFromCodesRequest
LabelFromCodesRequest.description:
Create labels with explicit short_codes (e.g. equipment serials).

Uniqueness is enforced per organization; a short_code already used in the
org (or duplicated within this request) is rejected with 409.

prefix.title: Prefix
prefix.description: Alphanumeric prefix for the short code (1-5 chars, e.g. STM, A, B12)

LabelPoolCreateDTO.title: LabelPoolCreateDTO
LabelPoolCreateDTO.description: Input DTO for CoreLabelsAPI.generate_pool — mirrors LabelPoolCreate fields.

LabelPoolListResponse.title: LabelPoolListResponse
LabelPoolListResponse.description: Paginated response for the label pool list endpoint.

LabelScanResponse.title: LabelScanResponse
LabelScanResponse.description:
The scan endpoint's published answer.

Same fields as the contract the providers build (``LabelScanDTO``); the
subclass keeps the component name this API has always published.

LanguageUpdate.title: LanguageUpdate
LanguageUpdate.description: Schema for updating user language preference.

LinkedReceiptSchema.title: LinkedReceiptSchema
LinkedReceiptSchema.description: Minimal document summary for linked receipts.

LlmCapability.title: LlmCapability
LlmCapability.description:
Tags describing what a connection can do.

Stored as ``list[str]`` JSONB on ``AiConnection``, so adding a new
capability tag is a no-op at the schema layer. The registry resolver
refuses connections whose ``capabilities`` list does not include the
purpose's required capability.

LocalizedText.title: LocalizedText
LocalizedText.description: A declared row's name and description in one language.

LocationCountState.title: LocationCountState
LocationCountState.description:
Where a location stands as a thing to count.

``last_counted_at`` is when the latest closed count that counted it
closed (empty: never counted); ``stock_take_id`` names the open count
covering it, when one is under way.

LocationLabelExport.title: LocationLabelExport
LocationLabelExport.description: Locations whose shelf labels to draw, and how: the preview and download.

LogoUploadResponse.title: LogoUploadResponse
LogoUploadResponse.description:
The stored org-scoped path of the uploaded logo.

Served back to the browser as ``/uploads/{logo_url}``; read server-side
by the PDF service for embedding.

LotLocationDTO.title: LotLocationDTO
LotLocationDTO.description: How much of one batch is standing in one place.

LotStatus.title: LotStatus
LotStatus.description:
Status values for ``StockLotDTO.status`` / ``StockLot.status``.

Only ``ACTIVE`` stock may be consumed, reserved or picked. Every other
value means the goods physically exist but are operationally held.

Lives here rather than in ``app.models`` so that modules — which the
import lint keeps out of ``app.models`` — can name the values of a field
the contract already hands them. Re-exported from
``app.models.stock_lot`` for callers on that import path.

LotStatusEventDTO.title: LotStatusEventDTO
LotStatusEventDTO.description:
One decision about a batch, as a person reads it.

The entry in ``meta_data['status_history']`` stores the author as a bare
UUID and the moment as an ISO string; the reader gets the name resolved
and the moment typed.

LotStatusUpdate.title: LotStatusUpdate
LotStatusUpdate.description:
Where the batch stands, and what the person was told.

The reason is required, for releases as much as for holds. Both halves
of that were argued: releasing a batch is a decision somebody will be
asked about, and one rule is easier to keep than a table of which
transitions need explaining. The friction is a sentence of typing, and
it buys the one thing a status alone cannot say — why.

Enforced here rather than in the service, because the module paths
(``quarantine_lot_async`` / ``release_lot_async``) are code acting on a
rule, not a person making a call, and have nobody to ask.

LowStockProduct.title: LowStockProduct
LowStockProduct.description: One product the tile's low-stock number counts — see ``low_stock``.

MarginResponse.title: MarginResponse
MarginResponse.description:
Read default margin for a template.

``is_default`` is ``True`` when the value comes from the system default,
not from a user-set ``meta_data['maker']['target_margin_pct']``.

MarginUpdate.title: MarginUpdate
MarginUpdate.description: Persist user's preferred target margin for a template.

MemberRoleUpdate.title: MemberRoleUpdate
MemberRoleUpdate.description:
A built-in level (``role``) or an org-scoped custom role (``role_id``).

Exactly one of the two: a member carries either a level from
``VALID_MEMBER_ROLES`` or one custom role — picking the enum clears the
custom links, picking a custom role replaces the previous one.

ModuleEnablePreview.title: ModuleEnablePreview
ModuleEnablePreview.description: What switching a module on would put into motion.

MonthlyResultItem.title: MonthlyResultItem
MonthlyResultItem.description: One month of the aggregated financial result (dashboard widget).

OpeningStockImportResponse.title: OpeningStockImportResponse
OpeningStockImportResponse.description:
What an opening-stock sheet became: one draft receipt, or nothing.

``document_id`` is None when no row could be read — no draft is left
behind for the reader to find empty. The counts and the refused rows
take the shape every spreadsheet import reports.

OrganizationAddress.title: OrganizationAddress
OrganizationAddress.description:
Structured issuer address.

``country`` is deliberately absent: the organization already has its own
ISO column — duplicating it here would recreate the free-text drift the
partner address migration removed.

OrganizationMemberCustomRole.title: OrganizationMemberCustomRole
OrganizationMemberCustomRole.description: The org-scoped custom role a member holds, if any.

OverdueAssignmentListResponse.title: OverdueAssignmentListResponse
OverdueAssignmentListResponse.description: Paginated response for the overdue-assignments list endpoint.

POSettingsSchema.title: POSettingsSchema
POSettingsSchema.description: Response schema for per-org PO approval settings.

POSettingsUpdate.title: POSettingsUpdate
POSettingsUpdate.description: Update payload for PO approval settings.

PackingLineOut.title: PackingLineOut
PackingLineOut.description: One document line, as far as packing has got with it.

text.title: Text
text.description: Raw text pasted from clipboard (Excel/Sheets). Delimiter (tab, comma, semicolon) is auto-detected.

PartnerAddress.title: PartnerAddress
PartnerAddress.description:
Structured partner address accepted on create/update.

``extra='forbid'`` rejects unknown keys so dead data never reaches the
JSONB column. ``country`` is an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (two uppercase
letters); :class:`PartnerAddressOut` is the lenient read shape that
tolerates legacy free-text country values already stored in the DB.

PartnerAddressOut.title: PartnerAddressOut
PartnerAddressOut.description:
Lenient read shape for a partner address.

``extra='allow'`` preserves unknown legacy keys instead of rejecting them,
and ``country`` may be a free-text value (e.g. "Polska") written before the
ISO alpha-2 migration. The frontend renders such values as "other: <value>".

PartnerImportResponse.title: PartnerImportResponse
PartnerImportResponse.description: What one partner import did; ``errors`` names the row and the reason.

PartnerListItem.title: PartnerListItem
PartnerListItem.description:
List item with document collaboration stats.

Aggregated in ``partner_service.list_partners_async`` from the
``documents`` table; zero-valued when no documents reference the partner.

PartnerPricelistCreate.title: PartnerPricelistCreate
PartnerPricelistCreate.description: Create a new supplier price list entry.

PartnerPricelistSchema.title: PartnerPricelistSchema
PartnerPricelistSchema.description: Response schema for a supplier price list entry.

PartnerPricelistUpdate.title: PartnerPricelistUpdate
PartnerPricelistUpdate.description: Patch an existing supplier price list entry.

PartnerUpdate.title: PartnerUpdate
PartnerUpdate.description: All fields optional — supports partial (PATCH-style) updates via PUT.

PasswordResetRequestOut.title: PasswordResetRequestOut
PasswordResetRequestOut.description:
What the reset-request endpoint can say without naming the account.

``email_delivery_configured`` describes the installation, not the address,
so it leaks nothing about who has an account here — and it is the
difference between "check your inbox" and a screen that waits for a letter
nobody will send.

PermissionUpdate.title: PermissionUpdate
PermissionUpdate.description: Request body for the permission-replace endpoint.

PickOrderStrategySchema.title: PickOrderStrategySchema
PickOrderStrategySchema.description:
One registered pick order, for the warehouse settings' chooser.

``label_key`` is where the owning module's catalogue holds the words for
it — the full form (``<module>:pickOrderStrategies.<name>``) the screen
reads and falls back to the bare name on. ``is_default`` marks the walk
used when nothing is chosen.

PlaceholderInfo.title: PlaceholderInfo
PlaceholderInfo.description:
A field a template author can print in a user template.

``key`` is the literal Jinja2 expression (e.g. ``{{partner.name}}``),
``example`` a representative rendered value, ``possibly_empty`` marks
fields that are absent for some documents, and ``document_types`` names
the document types the field belongs to (``None`` = any type).

PreviewIngredient.title: PreviewIngredient
PreviewIngredient.description: Parsed ingredient returned inside a recipe import preview.

PreviousMeasurement.title: PreviousMeasurement
PreviousMeasurement.description:
What the previous scheduled reconciliation pass measured.

The screen puts a row beside its predecessor with this — same figure
names as the report itself, plus when that pass ran. ``None`` on the
wire until the scheduled job has measured this organization once.

PriceHintResponse.title: PriceHintResponse
PriceHintResponse.description:
suggested unit price for a product on a document.

``source`` is ``pricelist`` (partner offer), ``last_purchase``
(most recent priced receipt) or ``None`` when no price is known.

PricingRequest.title: PricingRequest
PricingRequest.description: Compute sale price from cost + target margin for one template.

PricingResponse.title: PricingResponse
PricingResponse.description: Output — total cost, unit cost and suggested sale price.

PrintAgentRegister.title: PrintAgentRegister
PrintAgentRegister.description:
What an agent says about its printer when it starts.

An agent from before the label size moved to the job also sends
``media``, ``width_mm`` and ``height_mm``; they are ignored, not refused.
``agent_version`` and ``protocol_version`` are the opposite: an agent that
names no protocol is refused, because the server cannot tell what it
speaks and so cannot tell it from an agent it would refuse.

attempt.title: Attempt
attempt.description: Which claim of the job this is; the report carries it back.

PrintJobClaim.title: PrintJobClaim
PrintJobClaim.description: A job handed to an agent: print it before the lease runs out.

PrintJobCreate.title: PrintJobCreate
PrintJobCreate.description:
Labels to print: pool labels by id or short code, storage locations,
or products' barcode labels.

``agent_id`` may be left out while the organization has one printer.

attempt.title: Attempt
attempt.description: The attempt the claim named; an older claim is refused.

scale.title: Scale
scale.description: The share of their size the labels were printed at, when the printer could not hold them whole; left out when it could.

ProductLabelExport.title: ProductLabelExport
ProductLabelExport.description: Products whose barcode labels to draw, and how: the preview and download.

ProductProfile.title: ProductProfile
ProductProfile.description:
Minimal product profile definition.

Extended fields (route_overrides, nav_overrides, terminology) are deferred
until white-label / dominant-module requirements are clearer.

ProductSearchResult.title: ProductSearchResult
ProductSearchResult.description:
Result from product search endpoint.

Two searches share this shape. Without ``location_id`` the endpoint ranks
product templates, and ``item_id`` is absent. With one it ranks the stock
standing in that location, and every result names the item a dispatch line
has to reference — ``product_template_id`` is then whatever the item is
catalogued as, which may be nothing at all.

ProductTemplateClone.title: ProductTemplateClone
ProductTemplateClone.description: Schema for cloning a product template.

ProductTemplateCountResponse.title: ProductTemplateCountResponse
ProductTemplateCountResponse.description: Answer to "is the product catalog empty".

ProductTemplateCreate.title: ProductTemplateCreate
ProductTemplateCreate.description:
Request body for POST /items/product-templates.

Extends ProductTemplateBase (which carries name/brand/barcode/sku and
the descriptive fields) with the metadata payload the underlying model
supports. Kept on the schema (not just the service signature) so the
OpenAPI surface advertises it to the E2E seeding client.

organization_id.title: Organization Id
organization_id.description: None for global templates, UUID for org-specific

removal_strategy.title: Removal Strategy
removal_strategy.description: FIFO or FEFO; None follows the default (FIFO)

min_quantity.title: Min Quantity
min_quantity.description: Minimum stock threshold for low-stock alerts

meta_data.title: Meta Data
meta_data.description: Namespaced dict — modules use their own key

_weight_uom_dto.description: Eager-loaded weight UOM (opened-pack detection); None when the relationship is not loaded

ProductTemplateNutritionUpdate.title: ProductTemplateNutritionUpdate
ProductTemplateNutritionUpdate.description: Lightweight schema for updating only nutrition_info on a template.

ProductTemplateStockResponse.title: ProductTemplateStockResponse
ProductTemplateStockResponse.description:
How much of one product the organization has on its shelves.

The number a threshold is measured against, so the screen that sets
one can name it. That screen used to show the quantity of the single
record the reader had opened, and offered to copy it into a field
governing the product as a whole.

ProductionOrderCancel.title: ProductionOrderCancel
ProductionOrderCancel.description:
Optional request body for POST /orders/{id}/cancel.

``reason`` is stored on the order row and mirrored to the audit log.

ProductionOrderComplete.title: ProductionOrderComplete
ProductionOrderComplete.description:
Optional request body for POST /orders/{id}/complete.

``actual_qty`` is the real output quantity. When omitted, defaults to
``planned_qty`` (backward compatible). Must be > 0. When
``actual_qty > planned_qty``, the org's ``allow_overproduction`` setting
gates acceptance.

ProductionOrderCreate.title: ProductionOrderCreate
ProductionOrderCreate.description:
Input for POST /production/orders — DRAFT order to fulfil later.

Note: there is no ``input_storage_location_id`` — ingredients can be
drawn from multiple locations. Resolution happens at completion time
via ``stock_consumption.consume_across_locations``.

ProductionOrderLineRead.title: ProductionOrderLineRead
ProductionOrderLineRead.description: Snapshot of one consumed ingredient at completion time.

ProductionOrderUpdate.title: ProductionOrderUpdate
ProductionOrderUpdate.description:
Request body for PATCH /orders/{id} — all fields optional.

Only DRAFT orders can be updated; ``status``, ``output_template_id``
and ``output_storage_location_id`` are immutable after creation.

ProductionPreviewResponse.title: ProductionPreviewResponse
ProductionPreviewResponse.description:
Output for POST /production/orders/preview — what a run would take and cost.

The breakdown, plus what the person deciding needs before saving: each
ingredient's need against what the records hold where the run would draw
(``ingredients``, judged like completion judges), the recipe's batch size,
and the cost per unit with the recipe's fixed costs and the result against
its reference price.

ProductionStockMoveRead.title: ProductionStockMoveRead
ProductionStockMoveRead.description:
One stock move of a production run, named for display.

A module-local view over ``StockMoveDTO``: the core contract carries
identifiers, and resolving them to names is presentation, which belongs
to the module that presents them.

ProfileStorageLocation.title: ProfileStorageLocation
ProfileStorageLocation.description:
A starting location a product profile seeds for a new organization.

   Modules declare theirs in ``StorageLocationDeclaration``; a profile
   declares them here. Core seeds whatever the organization's profile asks
for and knows no location names of its own — before it hardcoded
   three on food storage types, so an organization on any other profile
   silently got none.

PurchaseOrderApprovalRequirement.title: PurchaseOrderApprovalRequirement
PurchaseOrderApprovalRequirement.description:
What confirming this order would do, for the person asking.

``approval_required`` says whether confirming goes to approval.
``approval_solvable`` is ``False`` where a request raised now, by confirming
or by asking for approval directly, would wait at a stage nobody could
decide for them, whether or not the rules require one; the two fields after
it say why, in the approvals module's stable codes, and which stage.

PurchaseOrderListRowSchema.title: PurchaseOrderListRowSchema
PurchaseOrderListRowSchema.description:
An order as the list shows it: its lines counted and summed.

``lines`` is empty unless the list was asked ``with_lines`` — the receive
screen, choosing which open order's lines to receive. The list itself
prints a count, the receipt progress per unit and the totals, summed in
the database: carried whole, the lines made a page of fifty orders
400 KB, and built only to be dropped, they stalled a page every few
requests.

PurchaseOrderUnitProgressSchema.title: PurchaseOrderUnitProgressSchema
PurchaseOrderUnitProgressSchema.description:
What an order's lines in one unit ordered and received, summed.

Kept per unit: 20 pcs and 12.5 kg are not 32.5 of anything.

PutawayCapacityCreate.title: PutawayCapacityCreate
PutawayCapacityCreate.description: One shelf's limit for one product, in the product's stock unit.

PutawayCapacityUpdate.title: PutawayCapacityUpdate
PutawayCapacityUpdate.description: Only the number moves; shelf and product are the entry's identity.

PutawayDo.title: PutawayDo
PutawayDo.description:
The shelf the goods were carried to — the suggestion, or another.

``scanned_code`` is the label the worker read at that shelf. The profile
may ask for it before the goods go on: the server resolves it then, so a
scan is something the shelf answered rather than something the screen
claims.

PutawayDone.title: PutawayDone
PutawayDone.description:
The posted move, and what the put-away has to say about the shelf.

``home_shelf`` is the offer to make the shelf the product's home (or why
it cannot be one); it is empty when nothing is to be asked.

PutawayLocationSettingOut.title: PutawayLocationSettingOut
PutawayLocationSettingOut.description: A location's product mix. Absent row reads mixed — the default.

PutawayOccupancyCell.title: PutawayOccupancyCell
PutawayOccupancyCell.description:
One shelf in the occupancy grid.

``fill`` is the shelf's fill in percent: the sum of every limited
product's share, the same sum the putaway planner decides by.
``status`` reads it as ``empty`` / ``no_limit`` / ``ok`` /
``nearly_full`` (from 85%) / ``over``; ``unmeasured`` says a product
stands here without a limit, so part of the shelf is not counted.
``capacity_used`` / ``capacity_max`` are the pair of the product taking
the largest share, and ``capacity_product_name`` says whose. All of
them are null on a shelf nobody limited — such a cell shows
``items_count`` instead of a percentage.

``entries`` lists every product on the shelf in the read of one
location. The overview of the whole floor lists the limited products
only — the segments of the bar — and the one product of a shelf that
holds one; ``products`` counts them all, and the reader asks the
location's own read for the rest.

PutawayOccupancyEntry.title: PutawayOccupancyEntry
PutawayOccupancyEntry.description:
One product on a shelf: what stands there against its limit.

Quantities speak the product's stock unit — the same unit the limit
was declared in, so the two compare without a conversion. ``share`` is
the product's part of the shelf in percent; the shelf's fill is the sum
of them. A product without a limit here has neither a limit nor a
share: it is unmeasured, not zero.

PutawayOccupancyNode.title: PutawayOccupancyNode
PutawayOccupancyNode.description:
One location of the occupancy tree, in walk order.

The list is depth first and each parent stands before its children, so a
reader folds a branch by skipping the rows deeper than it. ``cell`` is set
on a shelf (a location with nothing under it, or one that holds stock or
a limit itself); ``summary`` on a location that has others under it.

PutawayOccupancyOut.title: PutawayOccupancyOut
PutawayOccupancyOut.description: The occupancy read: every shelf under one location, and the signals.

PutawayOccupancyOverview.title: PutawayOccupancyOverview
PutawayOccupancyOverview.description:
Every warehouse and shelf of the organization in one answer.

The cells carry their fill, not their contents: a floor of two thousand
shelves holds hundreds of thousands of product groups, and sending them
all made the answer tens of megabytes and tens of seconds.

PutawayOccupancySignal.title: PutawayOccupancySignal
PutawayOccupancySignal.description:
A sentence the company overview quotes.

Two shapes behind one code field: a shelf that is nearly full names the
shelf and its fill; the count of receipt lines with nowhere to go names
only a count. The unused half stays null rather than becoming a second
endpoint.

PutawayOccupancySummary.title: PutawayOccupancySummary
PutawayOccupancySummary.description:
What a location holds, counted over the shelves under it.

``average_fill`` is taken over the shelves with a limit only — a shelf
nobody limited has no fill, and counting it as zero would make a
warehouse of unlimited shelves look empty. A shelf past its limit counts
as 100% there, so one overflow does not hide ten shelves with room.
``full`` includes the shelves over their limit.

PutawayPreviewLineIn.title: PutawayPreviewLineIn
PutawayPreviewLineIn.description:
One line of a receipt the receive screen has not saved yet.

The fields mirror what the executor reads off a document line: the
record (or catalogue product), the quantity in the unit it was stated
in, and the shelf the worker named over the plan.

PutawayPreviewLineOut.title: PutawayPreviewLineOut
PutawayPreviewLineOut.description:
Where one unsaved line will land, and who decided.

Named exactly as ``DocumentLine``'s plan fields so the same sentence
component and the same reading rule serve the saved document and the
form being filled in.

PutawayPreviewRequest.title: PutawayPreviewRequest
PutawayPreviewRequest.description:
Where a delivery is going, and the lines it brings.

``target_location_id`` is the document's destination — the shelf a rule
loses to and the one an unruled line lands on.

PutawayRuleCreate.title: PutawayRuleCreate
PutawayRuleCreate.description:
At least one match key and one target shelf must be set.

``location_ids`` is the rule's ordered list — the resolver walks it in
order, first fit wins. ``target_location_id`` still works and reads as
a list of one, so existing callers keep speaking the old shape; it is
the deprecated spelling.

PutawayRuleLocationOut.title: PutawayRuleLocationOut
PutawayRuleLocationOut.description: One shelf on a rule's ordered list, with its live state.

QuarantineHoldSchema.title: QuarantineHoldSchema
QuarantineHoldSchema.description:
Goods waiting for somebody to release them or write them off.

A named batch names itself. Goods held without one are named by the
receipt that placed them on the quarantine shelf and by the product the
decision is about, so the reader recognizes the row and reaches the
receipt or the shelf that holds it. The quantity is what is still held,
not what the receipt once set aside.

QuarantineTodoSection.title: QuarantineTodoSection
QuarantineTodoSection.description:
The quarantine holds in To do, with the server's own count.

A capped dashboard section, not a pageable list; see ``DocumentsTodoSection``.

ReceiptFromPOSchema.title: ReceiptFromPOSchema
ReceiptFromPOSchema.description:
Document created from a Purchase Order.

PO-local response schema — avoids importing ``DocumentSchema``
from the warehouse module.

ReceiptLineInput.title: ReceiptLineInput
ReceiptLineInput.description: Single line input for partial receipt.

ReceiptLineSchema.title: ReceiptLineSchema
ReceiptLineSchema.description: Document line returned within a receipt created from PO.

RecipeBridgeRead.title: RecipeBridgeRead
RecipeBridgeRead.description:
A snapshot from the culinary bridge, and who made it.

The bridge is idempotent: asking twice for the same output × source
pair hands back the first answer. A caller that abandons the second
half of the bridge needs to tell the two apart before cleaning up,
or it deletes a record somebody else was using.

RecipeCostLineRead.title: RecipeCostLineRead
RecipeCostLineRead.description: Output schema for a fixed cost line.

RecipeFromCulinaryCreate.title: RecipeFromCulinaryCreate
RecipeFromCulinaryCreate.description:
Input for POST /recipes/from-recipe — maker snapshot of a culinary recipe.

The culinary recipe (``source_recipe_id``, plain UUID without FK — the
recipes module may be disabled) is snapshotted into a new maker recipe
with BOM lines derived from its template-linked ingredients. The maker
recipe is frozen: later edits of the culinary recipe never propagate
(one-way snapshot).

RecipeList.title: RecipeList
RecipeList.description: Recipe in list view — lightweight, with availability badge.

RecipeRead.title: RecipeRead
RecipeRead.description: Output for GET /recipes/{id} — full recipe detail.

RecipeTagItem.title: RecipeTagItem
RecipeTagItem.description: A single tag with usage count and optional color.

ReconciliationResponse.title: ReconciliationResponse
ReconciliationResponse.description:
What the pair comparisons found, as the reader gets to see it.

Every figure the DTO carries is on the wire, including how much was
scanned to reach it — a drift of nought over nothing is not the same
statement as a drift of nought over eleven thousand records. The two
pairs that compared the records and their view with the quant table
ended with the table (ADR-022), and their fields with them.

RecordCookingRequest.title: RecordCookingRequest
RecordCookingRequest.description:
A step-by-step cook opens no picking session — nothing came off the
shelf. Recording it is what gives the cook its own entry (its own date
and servings) instead of lending the rating to whatever closed last.

``session_id`` is how a cook says it is not a new one: the step-by-step
screen opened after a picking run for the same dinner continues that
session instead of writing a second entry for one meal.

RegisterCurrencyTotal.title: RegisterCurrencyTotal
RegisterCurrencyTotal.description: Aggregated totals for one currency — sums are never mixed across currencies.

RegisterDocumentRow.title: RegisterDocumentRow
RegisterDocumentRow.description: Single document row in a register group.

RegisterGroup.title: RegisterGroup
RegisterGroup.description:
One group in the register summary (grouped by type/partner/location/month).

Carries the sums for the whole window, no rows — the documents come from
``GET /warehouse/register/rows`` one page at a time.

password.description: Password must be at least 8 characters with uppercase, lowercase, and digit

ReminderRunResult.title: ReminderRunResult
ReminderRunResult.description: What one press of Send Reminders did, and why it did no more.

ReorderRuleCreate.title: ReorderRuleCreate
ReorderRuleCreate.description:
Create a reorder rule for one (product, location) pair.

``min_quantity`` is the threshold that makes the rule fire; ``max_quantity``
is only the level to reach once it has. Requiredness used to be the other
way round -- MIN defaulted to 0 -- and the engine skips a rule at 0
outright, so a rule saved with the required fields alone could never
produce an alert while sitting on the list looking like every other one.

ReorderRuleSchema.title: ReorderRuleSchema
ReorderRuleSchema.description: Response schema for a reorder rule.

ReorderRuleUpdate.title: ReorderRuleUpdate
ReorderRuleUpdate.description:
Patch an existing reorder rule.

None means "leave it alone"; a value has to be one the engine can act on,
so a rule cannot be edited down into the state it cannot be created in.

ReplenishmentAlertDTO.title: ReplenishmentAlertDTO
ReplenishmentAlertDTO.description:
Stock-shortage alert for one (product, location) reorder rule.

Produced by ``purchase_orders.replenishment_service`` and exposed to
the documents stock router via ``purchase_orders_api`` so callers
never import internal module code. Mirrors the alert dict that the
UI consumed before this DTO existed.

ReplenishmentDraftPosCreate.title: ReplenishmentDraftPosCreate
ReplenishmentDraftPosCreate.description:
Request body for draft-PO creation from replenishment alerts.

The reorder rules whose current alerts should become draft purchase
orders — one DRAFT PO per distinct preferred supplier among them.

ReplenishmentDraftPosResult.title: ReplenishmentDraftPosResult
ReplenishmentDraftPosResult.description:
Result of the draft-from-alerts action: the orders created and
the requested rules left out, each with its reason.

ReplenishmentDraftSkipped.title: ReplenishmentDraftSkipped
ReplenishmentDraftSkipped.description:
A requested rule that did not become a PO line, with the reason.

``reason`` is a stable machine code the UI translates:
``not_found`` (no such rule in this org), ``not_alerting`` (stock is
at or above the minimum right now), ``covered_by_reserve`` (the
proposed internal move covers the whole shortage, so there is nothing
to buy), ``no_supplier`` (neither the rule nor the price list names
a supplier; reported, never turned into an empty order).

ReplenishmentMoveLineDTO.title: ReplenishmentMoveLineDTO
ReplenishmentMoveLineDTO.description:
One record a reserve replenishment would carry to a pick face.

The proposal is read by the warehouse module's To do action through
``purchase_orders_api``: it names the stock records, their shelf and
batch, so the transfer can be opened with its lines already prepared.

ReplenishmentProposalDTO.title: ReplenishmentProposalDTO
ReplenishmentProposalDTO.description: The internal move an alert proposes: what, from where, and how much.

RequesterLabel.title: RequesterLabel
RequesterLabel.description: One person or role a workflow holds, named for the card that lists it.

RequesterScope.title: RequesterScope
RequesterScope.description:
Whose submissions a workflow holds.

``everyone``, or the people and roles named — a role by the id the roles
list gives it, the built-in levels included. Anybody else's document,
order or checkout goes through without an approval. Choosing people and
naming nobody is refused rather than read as "nobody": a workflow that
holds nobody is a workflow switched off, and that is a different button.

ReturnLineCreate.title: ReturnLineCreate
ReturnLineCreate.description: A single line in a return request.

ReturnReasonCode.title: ReturnReasonCode
ReturnReasonCode.description: Why goods come back — same bargain as CorrectionReasonCode.

RoleCreate.title: RoleCreate
RoleCreate.description: Request body for creating a new org-scoped role.

RoleDTO.title: RoleDTO
RoleDTO.description: Named bundle of permissions assignable to a user.

RoleHolderDTO.title: RoleHolderDTO
RoleHolderDTO.description: Somebody who holds a role — enough to name them, and nothing more.

RoleRename.title: RoleRename
RoleRename.description: Request body for the rename endpoint.

ScopePreview.title: ScopePreview
ScopePreview.description:
What a scope holds before a campaign exists: the numbers the picker
and the launch confirmation both owe the reader, and the holders' names
a draft shows so the audience is more than a count.

ScrapReasonCode.title: ScrapReasonCode
ScrapReasonCode.description:
Why goods are written off — same bargain as CorrectionReasonCode.

A scrap that names no reason cannot answer "what did damaged goods cost
us" next to "what did expired goods cost us"; the code is what a report
groups by, the note says the rest.

SetBindingRequest.title: SetBindingRequest
SetBindingRequest.description:
Request body for ``PUT /ai-connections/bindings``.

``connection_id=None`` clears the binding — the UI offers an explicit
"not configured" option in the purpose dropdown.

SheetAnalysisResponse.title: SheetAnalysisResponse
SheetAnalysisResponse.description:
What the mapping step is told about an uploaded sheet.

Headers alone were not enough. The reader chose a mapping without seeing
a single value, so a sheet with a shifted header row — or one pandas split
on the wrong delimiter — looked correctly mapped, and the mismatch only
showed up after the rows had been written.

ShelfClosed.title: ShelfClosed
ShelfClosed.description: The answer to closing a shelf: how many rows it counted as none.

ShipmentCreate.title: ShipmentCreate
ShipmentCreate.description: The hand-over a dispatch's completion records beside its stock.

ShoppingListGenerationResult.title: ShoppingListGenerationResult
ShoppingListGenerationResult.description:
The result of generating a shopping list from a meal plan.

The outcome of an action: the list that was written and the counts that
explain it, with ``items`` the lines it just received. Not a collection
a client pages — the list itself is read from the shopping-list endpoints.

ShoppingSuggestionPreview.title: ShoppingSuggestionPreview
ShoppingSuggestionPreview.description:
What the app would propose buying — and nothing it has done.

Deliberately not ``ShoppingSuggestionResponse``: that one carries
``added``, and a preview adds nothing. Reporting a zero there would be
the same shape of untruth as the list this preview exists to stop
creating.

ShoppingSuggestionSchema.title: ShoppingSuggestionSchema
ShoppingSuggestionSchema.description: Schema for a single shopping suggestion.

ShortageItemRead.title: ShortageItemRead
ShortageItemRead.description:
One blocked ingredient — the refusal's own row.

Mirrors ``availability_service.ShortageItem`` so the order page can
read the exact list completion refuses with, instead of recomputing a
forecast that could disagree with it. ``shortage`` is null when the
line's measure and the stock's have no bridge: the ingredient still
blocks the run, but as "nobody can tell", not as a quantity.

ShortageShoppingListResponse.title: ShortageShoppingListResponse
ShortageShoppingListResponse.description:
Output for POST /production/orders/shortages/shopping-list.

The result of an action, not a collection: it names the list that was
touched and counts the lines added, and carries no rows to page.

StageDefinition.title: StageDefinition
StageDefinition.description:
One stage of a workflow: its name and the people who decide it.

An empty ``approver_user_ids`` is an open stage, decided by anyone who
holds the approve grant. Stages saved before this shape also carry a
``role`` — a free-form label that never decided anything — which the
schema now leaves out of what it reads and returns.

StatsConfig.title: StatsConfig
StatsConfig.description:
Module-level toggles every stats:read user may see.

Served from the module's own router because the generic settings endpoint
is admin-only, while the tab this drives is visible to viewers.

StockAsOfReportDTO.title: StockAsOfReportDTO
StockAsOfReportDTO.description:
What the warehouse held on a date, and what it was worth.

``complete_from`` is the boundary the ledger can answer from — the
oldest movement it holds. A date before it is refused rather than
answered: calm numbers for a year nothing was recorded in are more
dangerous than a refusal.

StockAsOfRowDTO.title: StockAsOfRowDTO
StockAsOfRowDTO.description: One product, as it stood on a given day.

StockLotDetailDTO.title: StockLotDetailDTO
StockLotDetailDTO.description:
A batch with the two things a recall asks for beyond its own fields.

``on_hand`` and ``locations`` come from the records, not from replaying
the ledger: the shelf is its own record, and the point of putting the
two next to each other is that a reader can see whether they agree.

StockMoveRowDTO.title: StockMoveRowDTO
StockMoveRowDTO.description:
A movement as a person reads it, not as five identifiers.

The names are read in the same statement as the row (see
``stock_moves_service.list_rows_for_org_async``): resolving them per row
would cost five lookups a row on a page of up to five hundred.

Every one of them is optional because the movement it describes may not
have that end at all — a delivery from outside has no origin, a product
without batches has no batch, and a row written by a background path has
nobody's name on it. What the source *is* stays ``reference_type`` and
``reference_id``: naming a document means reading a table Core must not
import.

StockQuantRowDTO.title: StockQuantRowDTO
StockQuantRowDTO.description:
A shelf as a person reads it, not as five identifiers.

Deliberately not a subclass of :class:`StockQuantDTO`: that one carries
``available_quantity`` as a Python property, which a response model does
not serialise, and the whole point of this row is that the promise is a
column of its own.

The names are read in the same statement as the row — resolving them per
row would cost four lookups a row on a page of five hundred.

force_over_tolerance.title: Force Over Tolerance
force_over_tolerance.description: Accept differences beyond the stock take tolerance

force_over_cap.title: Force Over Cap
force_over_cap.description: Allow counted quantities to exceed the growth cap

StockTakeCountRead-Input.title: StockTakeCountRead
StockTakeCountRead-Input.description: One pass of counting over one row, as the screens read it.

StockTakeCountRead-Output.title: StockTakeCountRead
StockTakeCountRead-Output.description: One pass of counting over one row, as the screens read it.

location_id.description: ID of the storage location for stock take

tolerance_percent.description: Ignore discrepancies up to this percent

require_full_count.title: Require Full Count
require_full_count.description: Require all items counted before finalize

StockTakeDiscrepancyCode.title: StockTakeDiscrepancyCode
StockTakeDiscrepancyCode.description:
Why a counted quantity differs from what the system held.

Free text answers "what happened on this shelf" and nothing else. It
cannot answer the question a warehouse asks after every count — how much
of the loss is breakage, how much is theft, how much is somebody putting
the goods on the wrong shelf — because twenty spellings of "broken" do
not add up. So the difference carries a code from this list, and a note
for what the list cannot say.

The vocabulary is the one warehouse systems settled on for shrink
categories: damage, expiry, loss, a miscount, goods found in the wrong
place, a unit that was read wrong, and a movement that never reached the
records. OTHER is the escape hatch, and the note stops being optional
whenever it is chosen — otherwise the escape hatch is the answer nobody
can read.

discrepancy_reason.title: Discrepancy Reason
discrepancy_reason.description: What the code does not say (required when the code is OTHER)

StockTakeItemCountUpdate.title: StockTakeItemCountUpdate
StockTakeItemCountUpdate.description: Schema for quick counting of a single item.

StockTakeItemCreate.title: StockTakeItemCreate
StockTakeItemCreate.description: Schema for creating stock take items.

StockTakeItemResponse.title: StockTakeItemResponse
StockTakeItemResponse.description: Response schema for stock take items.

StockTakeItemWithDetails.description: Stock take item schema with additional details.

StockTakeStatusUpdate.title: StockTakeStatusUpdate
StockTakeStatusUpdate.description: Schema for changing stock take status.

StockTakeWithDetails.description: Stock take schema with additional details.

StorageArchiveRequest.title: StorageArchiveRequest
StorageArchiveRequest.description:
«Move content and close» payload.

``move_items_to`` is required when the location (or any of its
descendants) still holds items; the archive then relocates them in the
same operation.

StorageCodeReprint.description: A location whose sticker still carries the code it had before numbering.

StorageCodeTemplateUpdate.title: StorageCodeTemplateUpdate
StorageCodeTemplateUpdate.description: A warehouse's code template; empty or null to follow the profile again.

StorageCodes.title: StorageCodes
StorageCodes.description: How a warehouse makes its location codes, and what waits to be relabelled.

StorageHierarchyCreate.title: StorageHierarchyCreate
StorageHierarchyCreate.description:
Atomically create a chain of locations of any length (ADR-018).

``steps`` walks downwards from ``parent_id``; every field below it
describes the **last** step, which is the location the caller is really
creating. Finishing higher up is a shorter chain, not a null name.

StorageHierarchyStep.title: StorageHierarchyStep
StorageHierarchyStep.description:
One node of a location chain: an existing one, or one to create.

``id`` names a node that already exists. ``name`` resolves to the child
of the previous step that carries it, and creates it when there is none.

StorageLocationNode.title: StorageLocationNode
StorageLocationNode.description: Tree node — used by GET /locations/tree endpoint.

StorageMoveScope.title: StorageMoveScope
StorageMoveScope.description: What one move of a batch carries with it, read on the batch's final tree.

StorageReorgOperation.title: StorageReorgOperation
StorageReorgOperation.description:
Single operation in a storage reorganization batch.

``parent_id`` accepts an existing location UUID, a ``temporary_id``
defined by an earlier ``create`` in the same batch, or ``None`` (root).

StorageReorgRejection.title: StorageReorgRejection
StorageReorgRejection.description: One rejected operation with its position in the batch and the reason.

StorageReprintedRequest.title: StorageReprintedRequest
StorageReprintedRequest.description: Locations whose new sticker is on the shelf now.

StorageTypeCreateDTO.title: StorageTypeCreateDTO
StorageTypeCreateDTO.description:
Input DTO for CoreStorageTypesAPI.create — mirrors StorageTypeCreate fields.

``field_definitions`` uses ``list[dict[str, Any]]`` (not the internal
``CategoryFieldDefinition`` model) to stay contracts-legal; the CoreAPI maps

StorageTypeInlineCreate.title: StorageTypeInlineCreate
StorageTypeInlineCreate.description: Storage type passed inline — created atomically within StorageHierarchyCreate.

StorageTypeUpdateDTO.title: StorageTypeUpdateDTO
StorageTypeUpdateDTO.description:

Mirrors StorageTypeUpdate; unset fields are excluded from the update via
``model_dump(exclude_unset=True)`` inside CoreAPI.

TagColorRequest.description:
A tag's colour, or ``null`` for no colour at all.

``null`` is a value here, not a missing field: the tag manager has offered
a "clear colour" button since it was written, and with ``color: str`` the
only reply that button could ever get was a 422. The column has always
been nullable — it was the API that refused.

TargetType.title: TargetType
TargetType.description: A thing an approval workflow can be attached to.

TemplatePreviewRequest.title: TemplatePreviewRequest
TemplatePreviewRequest.description: A layout to render, as the editor currently has it.

TemplatePreviewResponse.title: TemplatePreviewResponse
TemplatePreviewResponse.description: The layout rendered onto the example document.

TestConnectionRequest.title: TestConnectionRequest
TestConnectionRequest.description:
Request body for ``POST /ai-connections/test``.

Either pass ``connection_id`` (test an existing row, in which case the
stored cipher is used) OR the inline fields (test a draft before saving,
in which case ``api_key`` is plaintext). The router validates that one
of the two modes is present.

Token.title: Token
Token.description:
Login/refresh response.

The refresh token is deliberately absent: it lives in the HttpOnly
``refresh_token`` cookie only, out of reach of page scripts.

UnitMismatch.title: UnitMismatch
UnitMismatch.description:
Both readings, when the recipe's measure and the shelf's cannot meet.

Handed over instead of a consumed quantity: with nothing recording how

UnlinkedIngredient.description: One unlinked ingredient, with enough context to recognise it.

lookup returns.

UomInfoWithCategory.description: The embedded UoM plus the category name, as item responses carry it.

WorkItemSchema.title: WorkItemSchema
WorkItemSchema.description:
A task, with the one next action and the record that action opens.

``state`` is read from what has happened to the source, never typed in:
nothing recorded is ``todo``, an open session or recorded quantities is
``in_progress``, a source posted or recorded in the last day is ``done``
(listed only when asked for), and a cancelled one is no longer a task.
A custom task is ``done`` when it is ticked, which nothing else can say.

WorkflowConfigured.title: WorkflowConfigured
WorkflowConfigured.description:
Whether a request for this target type would land anywhere.

``True`` is the engine's own test before it writes a request: an
active workflow with at least one stage. Both refusals are covered
here — no active workflow (``approval_no_active_workflow``) and an
active one with no stages (``approval_workflow_no_stages``) — so the
screen that offers the request button and the endpoint that receives
it are one rule, asked twice.

expected_scope.description: The scope the switch-on dialog showed: the `scope` of the workflow as the workflow list returns it. Required with `is_active: true` wherever the target type says what a workflow holds (422 `APPROVAL_SCOPE_REQUIRED`, naming this field, otherwise), so a script cannot bring a workflow into force under a rule it never read. The server answers 409 `APPROVAL_SCOPE_CHANGED` when the live scope differs. Not needed for a target type with no scope provider, for switching off, or for editing a workflow that is already on. The scope is readable from the list only, so a client creates the workflow off, reads its scope, then switches it on.

WorkflowDeletionResult.title: WorkflowDeletionResult
WorkflowDeletionResult.description:
What became of a workflow the user asked to delete.

``archived`` means it was kept because requests were already raised
under it: it is off the list, frozen, and a new workflow for its target
type is a new row. ``requests_kept`` counts those requests.

WorkflowScope-Input.title: WorkflowScope
WorkflowScope-Input.description:
What an active workflow for a target type holds, in the owner's words.

Answered by the module that owns the target and its gate, so the sentence
an administrator reads before switching a workflow on is the rule the
gate then applies. ``all`` with no ``required_by_settings`` is the
workflow itself being the rule (the settings name nothing); ``nothing``
is a workflow that holds nothing until the module's settings ask.
``required_by_settings`` names the settings that demand an approval of
their own, whatever the workflow.

WorkflowScopeCondition-Input.title: WorkflowScopeCondition
WorkflowScopeCondition-Input.description:
One filter a module's settings put on what a workflow holds.

``document_types`` lists the kinds always held; ``value_above`` holds
whatever is worth more than ``amount`` (in ``currency``) and, with
``unpriced_included``, whatever has no value to compare;
``foreign_currency`` holds anything priced in another currency than the
organization's, which no threshold can be compared with.
